<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro primo Regum
<r>1 Reg 2:27-29</r>
<n>27</n> Venit autem vir Dei ad Heli, et ait ad eum: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Numquid non apérte revelátus sum dómui patris tui, cum essent in Ægýpto in domo Pharaónis?
<n>28</n> Et elégi eum ex ómnibus tríbubus Israël mihi in sacerdótem, ut ascénderet ad altáre meum, et adoléret mihi incénsum, et portáret ephod coram me: et dedi dómui patris tui ómnia de sacrifíciis filiórum Israël.
<n>29</n> Quare calce abiecístis víctimam meam, et múnera mea quæ præcépi ut offerréntur in templo: et magis honorásti fílios tuos quam me, ut comederétis primítias omnis sacrifícii Israël pópuli mei?
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Præparáte corda vestra Dómino, et servíte illi soli:
* Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.
<r>℣.</r> Convertímini ad eum in toto corde vestro, et auférte deos aliénos de médio vestri.
<r>℟.</r> Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the first book of Samuel
<r>1 Sam 2:27-29</r>
<n>27</n> And there came a man of God to Heli, and said to him: Thus saith the Lord: Did I not plainly appear to thy father's house, when they were in Egypt in the house of Pharao?
<n>28</n> And I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, and burn incense to me, and to wear the ephod before me: and I gave to thy father's house of all the sacrifices of the children of Israel.
<n>29</n> Why have you kicked away my victims, and my gifts which I commanded to be offered in the temple: and thou hast rather honoured thy sons than me, to eat the firstfruits of every sacrifice of my people Israel?
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve Him Only
* And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.
<r>℣.</r> Return unto Him with all your hearts, and put away the strange gods from among you.
<r>℟.</r> And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>1 Reg 2:30-33</r>
<n>30</n> Proptérea ait Dóminus Deus Israël: Loquens locútus sum, ut domus tua, et domus patris tui, ministráret in conspéctu meo usque in sempitérnum. Nunc autem dicit Dóminus: Absit hoc a me: sed quicúmque glorificáverit me, glorificábo eum: qui autem contémnunt me, erunt ignóbiles.
<n>31</n> Ecce dies véniunt, et præcídam brácchium tuum, et brácchium domus patris tui, ut non sit senex in domo tua.
<n>32</n> Et vidébis ǽmulum tuum in templo, in univérsis prósperis Israël: et non erit senex in domo tua ómnibus diébus.
<n>33</n> Verúmtamen non áuferam pénitus virum ex te ab altári meo: sed ut defíciant óculi tui, et tabéscat ánima tua: et pars magna domus tuæ moriétur cum ad virílem ætátem vénerit.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Percússit Saul mille, et David decem míllia:
* Quia manus Dómini erat cum illo: percússit Philisthǽum, et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Nonne iste est David, de quo canébant in choro, dicéntes: Saul percússit mille, et David decem míllia?
<r>℟.</r> Quia manus Dómini erat cum illo: percússit Philisthǽum, et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>1 Sam 2:30-33</r>
<n>30</n> Wherefore thus saith the Lord the God of Israel: I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father should minister in my sight, for ever. But now saith the Lord: Far be this from me: but whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify: but they that despise me, shall be despised.
<n>31</n> Behold the days come: and I will cut off thy arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thy house.
<n>32</n> And thou shalt see thy rival in the temple, in all the prosperity of Israel, and there shall not be an old man in thy house for ever.
<n>33</n> However I will not altogether take away a man of thee from my altar: but that thy eyes may faint and thy soul be spent: and a great part of thy house shall die when they come to man's estate
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, in te sperántium fortitúdo, adésto propítius invocatiónibus nostris: et, quia sine te nihil potest mortális infírmitas, præsta auxílium grátiæ tuæ; ut, in exsequéndis mandátis tuis, et voluntáte tibi et actióne placeámus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.c7a463e2e0:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, the Strength of all them that put their trust in thee, mercifully accept our prayers, and because through the weakness of our mortal nature we can do no good thing without thee, grant us the help of thy grace, that in keeping of thy commandments we may please thee, both in will and deed.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.c82e5deee0:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uarto Kaléndas Iúnii Luna vicésima tértia. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>anctæ Maríæ-Magdalénæ de Pazzis, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Vírginis, cuius dies natális octávo Kaléndas Iúnii recensétur.
<h>R</h>omæ, via Aurélia, natális sancti Restitúti Mártyris.
<h>A</h>pud Icónium, in Lycaónia, pássio sanctórum Conónis, et fílii annórum duódecim, qui, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre, cratículæ, prunis suppósitis et óleo superinfúso candéntis, suspensiónis in equúleo atque ignis pœnam constánter passi, ad extrémum, málleo ligneo mánibus eórum contrítis, spíritum emisérunt.
<h>I</h>n agro Tridentíno natális sanctórum Mártyrum Sisínii, Martýrii et Alexándri; qui, témpore Honórii Imperatóris, in Anáuniæ pártibus (ut scribit in vita sancti Ambrósii Paulínus), persequéntibus Gentílibus, martýrii corónam adépti sunt.
<h>C</h>ameríni pássio sanctórum mille quingentórum et vigínti quinque Mártyrum.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ Philíppi sanctárum Mártyrum Theodósiæ, quæ sancti Procópii Mártyris éxstitit mater, et aliárum duódecim nobílium matronárum; quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cápitis obtruncatióne consummátæ sunt.
<h>T</h>réviris beáti Maximíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; a quo sanctus Athanásius Epíscopus, ob persecutiónem Arianórum éxsulans, honorífice suscéptus fuit.
<h>V</h>erónæ sancti Máximi Epíscopi.
<h>A</h>rcáni, in Látio, sancti Eleuthérii Confessóris.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.be697854ca:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>ay 29th 2027, the 23rd day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Virgin Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi, of the Order of Carmelites, famous for her holy life, of whom mention is made upon the 25th day of the month of May.
<h>U</h>pon the same 29th day of May, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the holy martyr Restitutus.
<h>A</h>t Iconium, a city of Isauria, the holy martyrs Conon and his son aged twelve years. Under the Emperor Aurelian they suffered with great firmness from being basted with oil upon a grating over live coals, stretching upon the rack and fire, and at length gave up the ghost as their hands were being pounded with a wooden mallet.
<h>O</h>n the same day, the holy martyrs Sisinius, Martyrius, and Alexander, who are stated by Paulinus, in his life of holy Ambrose, to have gained the crown of martyrdom in the parts of Val-d'Anagna, under the persecution of the heathen in the time of the Emperor Honorius.
<h>I</h>n Umbria suffered one thousand five hundred and twenty-five holy martyrs.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea Philippi, the holy martyrs Theodosia, mother of the holy martyr Procopius, and twelve other noble matrons, who were beheaded in the persecution under Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Trier, the blessed Confessor Maximin, Bishop [of that city,] who honourably welcomed the holy Bishop Athanasius when he was in exile from the persecution of the Arians.
<h>A</h>t Verona, [in the fourth century,] the holy Maximus, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>A</h>t Arci, in Latium, the holy Confessor Eleutherius.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
